title: OpenAI ChatCompletions conformance proxy with streaming + tool-hook mapping
creator: Ava Morales
description: Build a lightweight compatibility proxy that accepts OpenAI ChatCompletions v1-style requests and translates them to Redwood API calls (and vice versa). The proxy must: handle streaming chunk translation, preserve role/content/metadata mapping, implement function/tool calling semantics (including tools metadata and return values), enforce structured-output contract (content-type + JSON validation), and return OpenAI-like errors and status codes. It should support two modes: permissive (best-effort mapping with warnings) and strict (reject incompatible constructs). The goal is to provide a drop-in shim for customers migrating from OpenAI to Redwood without changing existing client code while maintaining Redwood runtime performance and telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts typical OpenAI ChatCompletions request payloads and returns semantically equivalent Redwood responses for non-streaming flows
Streaming mode: server-sent events / chunked responses are translated to OpenAI-style delta events and include function call tokens when applicable
Tool/function calling: function call request fields (name, arguments) map to Redwood tool invocation and response payloads are surfaced back as function call content
Structured outputs: schema hints in OpenAI-style messages are enforced; invalid JSON in strict mode results in a well-formed error response
HTTP status and error codes mirror OpenAI semantics for common errors (rate limit, invalid request, model not found)
Telemetry: request/response mapping includes trace IDs and adds mapping metadata to Redwood logs for debugging
Performance: added proxy latency under 10ms p50 and <30ms p95 in canary tests under typical load
Comprehensive integration tests for streaming, tool-calling, and structured output scenarios exist and run in CI
comments: 2026-02-20 - Ava Morales: Created ticket with initial scope after customer support calls where migration broke streaming tool calls.

2026-02-24 - Jun Park: Spike complete. Confirmed approach: single proxy component that rewrites request body and subscribes to Redwood streaming API; uses an adapter layer to emit OpenAI-style deltas.

2026-02-27 - Jun Park: Identified tricky edge case: OpenAI stream may emit 'function_call' as a series of partial deltas. Need assembly logic to deterministically reconstruct function name + args before emitting final function_call event. Added unit tests.

2026-03-02 - Design review (Lena Ortiz): UX for error messages when strict mode rejects structured-output validated payloads approved. Use OpenAI-style error object with code+message and include validation diagnostics URL.
2026-03-04 - PR #4512: initial implementation pushed to repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-proxy/pull/4512
2026-03-06 - Infra (Samir Gupta): Requested circuit-breaker + retry policy to avoid cascading failures from downstream tool integrations. Added config knobs to proxy runtime.

2026-03-08 - QA (Maya Chen): Started integration test harness that replays recorded OpenAI sessions (streaming + tool calls). Found a bug when function args contain nested JSON with escaped newlines — fixed in branch and added test case.

2026-03-10 - Jun Park: Canary started in us-west-2 for a small set of customers. Observability dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/proxy-compat-canary. Initial latency p50 +5ms vs baseline, p95 +22ms. Monitoring look OK. Next: broad canary and docs update.
Follow-ups: add opt-in telemetry flag for mapping verbosity; coordinate with legal/security for audit of tool call payload persistence in proxy logs.
implementation_notes: Adapter layers: request-adapter (OpenAI->Redwood) and response-adapter (Redwood->OpenAI) to keep logic testable
Streaming assembly: buffer partial deltas for function_call until closing token is detected or timeout (200ms) elapses
Schema enforcement: integrate existing Redwood Evaluate schema validator; in strict mode reject before calling model to save compute
Error mapping table: maintain a map from Redwood internal error codes -> OpenAI HTTP 4xx/5xx classes with example messages
Telemetry: inject X-Redwood-Compat-ID and preserve OpenAI 'id' in proxied responses where possible
Security: redact sensitive tool arguments in logs by default; add KMS-backed config for exceptions
testing_plan: Unit tests for adapters with edge cases (escaped JSON, large function args, role-only messages)
Integration tests that run end-to-end against a staging runtime using replayed OpenAI traffic
Load tests to validate latency budget under mixed streaming and non-streaming traffic
Canary rollout with circuit-breaker and automatic rollback on error spike
User acceptance: invite 3 customers on migration path to opt into canary and collect qualitative feedback
rollout_plan: feature branch -> internal staging -> canary (10 customers) -> expanded canary (50 customers) -> GA
Monitoring SLOs: error rate <0.5% and stream reconnection <0.2% during canary
Docs: migration guide + mapping examples for common Python/Node client patterns
Post-mortem within 72 hours for any canary >SLA violation
